# The Finding Ledger — lessons with their extensions

<!-- Generated by kstack-init on {{DATE}} for {{PROJECT_NAME}}. The starter lessons below are
     IMPORTED: their statements travelled from the origin repo; their evidence did not. Each
     earns local members at this repo's unit closes — an imported statement that never earns a
     member here may eventually be pruned at a close, with a written reason. -->

**What this is.** The home of the repo's build lessons, kept in the form Bennett's razor demands
(*"explanations should be no more specific than necessary"* — arXiv:2301.12987): each lesson is
the **weakest statement still sufficient** to correctly decide every finding in its
**extension** (the recorded defects it forbids). AGENTS.md holds the *procedure*; lessons and
their evidence accrete HERE, so the procedure file stays a fixed size.

**How it is used** (the unit-close step, AGENTS.md step 5b). When a round's findings are
clustered, look each cluster up here first:

- **Covered but unenforced** — an existing lesson's extension already decides it. The statement
  was right; its MEDIUM failed. Promote the medium (prose → checklist field → lint / Record /
  registry walk / DB trigger). Do not touch the statement.
- **Not covered** — the standing lesson is TOO STRONG. Weaken the statement until the new member
  falls inside, then re-run the sufficiency walk over ALL its members.
- **No lesson claims it** — mint one: the weakest statement sufficient over the cluster AND any
  historical findings it also decides. Land it in the most quantification-forcing medium that
  can express it; prose-only requires a written reason.

**The sufficiency walk** keeps this from being taste: for every finding in a claimed extension,
one sentence — "applied at build time, this forbids that defect because …". A member you cannot
write the sentence for is not in the extension.

**Media, ranked by quantification force** (why: a Record/walk/trigger can only say "EVERY member
of the family…", which is a weak hypothesis whose extension includes members that do not exist
yet — the reason mechanized lessons hold under attack and prose ones leak):
`DB constraint/trigger` > `registry walk / compile-forced Record` > `lint rule` > `required
design-artifact field` > `gate-rubric line` > `prose (with reason)`.

## The lessons (imported starter set — extensions empty, earned locally)

### L1 — Carry the fact; never infer it from a co-occurring value
A fact a consumer must act on is carried as its own positive record from the layer that first
has it. The presence, absence, or shape of an ADJACENT value is never a discriminant — a
discriminant comes from the structure that produced the object.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}). *Origin note: the origin repo's
  highest-regeneration lesson — five members across three eras.*
- **Medium:** prose (imported).

### L2 — A recurrent domain act needs occurrence identity
Any act that can happen twice (capture, acknowledgement, booking, webhook delivery) needs an
identity a second occurrence can be told apart by — a key, its own row, or an event carrying the
key. A scalar/state projection cannot deduplicate, correct, or replay.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported).

### L3 — Requiredness is a property of the fact's journey
A fact is required at EVERY boundary between where it is established and every consumer that
must act on it. "Optional so existing callers/fixtures compile" is never a reason; the churn is
the diagnostic and is paid in the same commit.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported; also stated in AGENTS.md Build Principles).

### L4 — An invariant is enforced where every writer passes
An invariant over mutable facts is stated against its full WRITER SET, enumerated in the same
commit — and enforced at a point all of them cross (the database, when the writers cannot all
be seen). A birth-time or single-site check on a journey invariant is a defect waiting for the
second writer.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported).

### L5 — Family side effects live in a structure the writers iterate
When N writers each owe the same family of side effects, the family is a compile-forced
Record/table/chokepoint the writers iterate — never N hand-maintained call-site lists. The
trigger is the SECOND writer, not the third regression.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported).

### L6 — The enforcement-tier law
What must hold for every writer holds in the DATABASE; the type system is ergonomics for the
writers the compiler can see; a comment is a record, not an enforcement. (This is also the
close step's own medium-selection rule.)
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported; also stated in AGENTS.md Build Principles).

### L7 — Absence is a named variant
Where absence is a genuine domain state it is a NAMED variant (`carried | none | unavailable`),
never `undefined`, an empty array dereference, or a silent fallback.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported).

### L8 — A projection must not alter a validated fact
Rounding, formatting, labelling, or any derived view happens AFTER validation only if the
projected value is re-validated (or the exact value is kept and projection is display-only). A
monitor/view that contradicts the ledger is a claim to diagnose, never ground truth.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported).

### L9 — A test must be able to express the attack
A test that stubs the thing under test is a test of the stub; a fixture that cannot express the
attack makes the property unwritable in that file; an assertion must reach the OUTCOME, not stop
at the seam. Corollary: a fixture family that cannot express a dimension BOUNDS where
enforcement can live — record that bound when you meet it.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported).

### L10 — A queue is a work list
Pile membership = the POSITIVE undone-work fact on a LIVE parent, and the card lands on the desk
that carries the queue's verb. A pile must never point at a verb that refuses.
- **Extension:** none locally (imported {{DATE}}).
- **Medium:** prose (imported).

## Loop health

One row per gated unit, appended by the close-unit step. `novel n/m` = statements minted vs
total findings (the loop's health metric: mostly re-samplings ⇒ the problem is media, not
doctrine). `mode:` = whether the gate ran FED (ledger in the rubric) or BLIND — the gate script
SELF-SCHEDULES a blind CONTROL round every 4th unit by counting `mode: fed` rows since the last
`mode: blind` row in this table (no human keeps the count; `--with-ledger` / `--no-ledger`
override one run). If blind rounds keep finding what fed rounds stopped finding, the feed is
anchoring (drop the hunt clause, keep the disclosure rule); if both converge on the same
shrinking set, the feed is innocent.

(no rows yet — the first gated unit's close appends the first)

## Ledger discipline

One lesson per statement; extensions cite probes by number; a regenerated finding is FIRST a
diagnosis (which fork above), only then a fix. When a lesson is fully mechanized, its AGENTS.md
prose (if any) is CUT to a one-line pointer — that is the graduation rule that keeps AGENTS.md
from bloating. Unit-close records live in the unit's own probe (§ "Close of unit"); this file
holds only the distilled lessons.
